area: A scope amendment reaches the ledger and the direction lock but not the work-admission ticket grant
finding: tasks scope add now unions the new path into both scopePaths and taskDirectionLock.allowedFiles — the ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-007 fix, confirmed live. It does not reseal the work-admission ticket, and the ticket's file-write grant is what git commit --auto-stage resolves the delivery bundle from. The next governed commit therefore stages the pre-amendment bundle, omits the file the amendment was requested for, and reports ATM_GIT_COMMIT_OK. The commit is not wrong about anything it did; it is silent about what it left out, which is the one file the operator had just asked to include.
expectedBehavior: An accepted scope amendment must land in every representation that a later governed operation reads as authority, the ticket grant included, or scope add must refuse until the ticket can be resealed. Failing that, a delivery commit whose resolved bundle is narrower than the task's current scope must say so rather than report unqualified success.
evidenceOrRepro: ATM-GOV-0366, 2026-08-13. tasks scope add added docs/governance/atm-bug-and-optimization-backlog.items/ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-022.json and reported ATM_SCOPE_AMENDMENT_APPLIED; the ledger showed the path in both scopePaths and taskDirectionLock.allowedFiles. The immediately following git commit --auto-stage returned ATM_GIT_COMMIT_OK as b0a11e666, whose tree contains ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-021.json and the ledger bundle but not 022, which git status still reported as untracked. taskflow pre-close then blocked with ATM_WRITE_TICKET_SCOPE_VIOLATION and prescribed tasks renew, which resealed the ticket and let a second commit carry the file.
followUp: Reseal the ticket inside the scope-amendment transaction, so the amendment is atomic across ledger, direction lock and ticket exactly as [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-017] requires of claim identity. The detection layer already works — pre-close named the violation and prescribed the correct recovery — so the gap is that the commit ran between the amendment and the reseal without noticing it was using a stale grant. This is the same family as [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-007]: that fix taught the amendment to reach two of the three representations, and the third was not known to be load-bearing until an amendment landed mid-delivery. One further observation from the same recovery, mechanism not established and therefore not claimed: the second tasks renew minted a fresh lane session and offered it as the requested lane while ATM_LANE_SESSION_ID was exported and unchanged, producing ATM_TASK_CLAIM_OWNER_MISMATCH with the same actor id printed on both sides. The first renew, in an identical shell minutes earlier, had honoured the exported lane. lane adopt on the holding lane, which the refusal named outright, recovered it. Relevant to [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-018], which records that claim entry points disagree about lane resolution.
